reason: Bridge->Reasoning, forward framing rather than factual invalidation. reasoning_because (Micron's fiscal-Q3-2026 print of 2026-06-25) remains true but is now the weakest of four supply-side anchors: validation.88f02c5e38fce41b (07-29, rel 4, landing) has SK Hynix stating in its own results that HBM gated what else the fab could produce, and validation.371702f0db42e614 (07-30, rel 5, so_that) has Samsung quantifying it -- 60% to 70% of capacity to be placed under long-term contract, constraints through 2028, and a wider 2027 supply-demand gap than 2026. Meanwhile validation.d6f4a8eaa52f7bca (07-31, rel 4) narrows the residual gap to a single distinction the current reasoning never draws: Amazon's Jassy said $220bn of 2026 capex will not meet demand and Olsavsky attributed the $20bn increase to memory cost -- naming memory as a cost driver, not as an allocation ceiling. Rewrite should re-anchor because on the 07-29/07-30 supplier disclosures and sharpen so_that to state explicitly that a cost complaint from a buyer does not satisfy the claim; only an allocation- or volume-denominated shipment limit does. The Q2 2027 landing window is unchanged.
